note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses), round 1. This item's 15-17 Oct review was not among the files recovered after the device move, so both lenses were reviewed afresh on the new device on 18 Oct 2026. Not yet acted on. compose.py switched to signature v2 during this review; F1 reports both v1 and v2.

item-quality.verdict: Solvable and fair to valid alternatives, but the oracle is too weak in two ways, so the item should not be accepted yet. What holds: a competent GNU Radio developer can solve it from the instruction and the empty start graph. Every number the oracle uses is stated: fs 50 kHz, the 90 % in-band share, the four 20-30 % quarters, the two < 1 % stopbands, RMS 0.6 +/- 5 %, the file name and item type, and 'keeps running until stopped' (the liveness need of 65536 items is covered). build/L1 is correct (4 blocks, single rate). The 18 Oct band_fraction fix does not affect this item: a correct output is complex, and a real capture still scores 0 in the negative band. Valid alternatives I wrote pass V6 with ./gb ladder: low-pass + Rotator, FFT Filter with complex_band_pass taps, and cutoffs read as -10.25/-1.75 kHz. The three variants pass, and the author's 300-seed sweep reproduces exactly. A wrong real-tap band-pass (fir_filter_ccf, 2-10 kHz) is rejected. What fails: (F2) the oracle cannot tell noise from deterministic signals. Four tones at -9/-7/-5/-3 kHz, or a -10..-2 kHz chirp, pass V6, although the instruction says 'Start from white Gaussian noise ... and filter it' (structural wording with no graph check). (F3) The instruction prescribes a design (input RMS 1.5, Gaussian, cutoffs, 500 Hz transition, unity gain) that V6 checks only through the output. Noise amp 1 with gain 1.5, uniform noise, and transition widths of 1000-1500 Hz all pass. Fix F2 (a tested path graph check), decide F3, and re-run the gates. Scratch: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-02/ (WSL; .grc counter-examples, run_alts.py, run_mutants.py, run_nearmiss.py, crest_sweep.py, task_with_*.json, repl/ build replica).

findings.claim: The oracle checks only where the output power lies and its RMS level, so answers that produce no noise at all pass V6. The instruction says 'Gaussian noise' and 'Start from white Gaussian noise ... and filter it'. Under the 16 Oct oracle policy that is structural wording and needs a graph check, but task.json has no oracle.graph_checks. A comb of four equal tones, one per 2 kHz quarter, or a linear chirp across -10..-2 kHz, satisfies every V6 check.
findings.evidence:
./gb ladder with items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-02/task.json:
- s1_four_tones.grc: four complex Signal Sources at -9, -7, -5 and -3 kHz, amplitude 0.3 each, then Add, Throttle and File Sink lower_band_noise.dat. No noise source, no filter. Result V6 PASS: in-band 0.99998, quarters 0.2500/0.2500/0.2501/0.2499, above -1 kHz 7e-6, below -11 kHz 1e-6, RMS 0.60004.
- s2_chirp.grc: a sawtooth (5 Hz, amp 8000, offset -10000) drives a Frequency Modulator (sensitivity 2*pi/samp_rate), then x0.6, Throttle and File Sink. Result V6 PASS: in-band 0.9937, quarters 0.244-0.256, RMS 0.599998.
Candidate fixes, tested on scratch copies of task.json:
(i) Graph check {kind: path, from_ids: [analog_noise_source_x, analog_fastnoise_source_x], via_ids: [band_pass_filter, low_pass_filter, fir_filter_xxx, fft_filter_xxx, interp_fir_filter_xxx, freq_xlating_fir_filter_xxx, freq_xlating_fft_filter_ccc, filter_fft_low_pass_filter, iir_filter_xxx, rational_resampler_xxx], to_ids: [blocks_file_sink]}. The reference, all 3 variants and the 3 extra valid alternatives (a1_rotator, a2b_fft_filter_default_window, a3_edges_outside) pass; s1 and s2 fail with 'no such path'.
(ii) A max_abs >= 1.4 check. crest_sweep.py, over 300 seeds, gives max|x|/rms of 2.74-4.16 for every accepted design, including uniform input, so max|x| >= 1.56 even at the lowest allowed RMS of 0.57. Four tones give 1.2 and the chirp 0.6. In the ladder the reference gives 1.79, the variants 1.99/2.06/2.06 and the alternatives 1.84-1.96; s1 and s2 fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the path graph check (i) to oracle.graph_checks (group main) with a spec property such as 'P11 the File Sink receives a noise source's output after a filter'. It enforces the instruction's own words and accepts every valid structure tried. Optionally add (ii) as a behavioural noise check. If so, the instruction must say it, for example 'the output must be random noise, not a set of tones or a sweep', so that the 1.4 threshold is not an unstated requirement. Re-run the gates, and keep s1/s2 as negative checks.

findings.claim: The instruction prescribes a design as requirements: 'white Gaussian noise with an RMS level of 1.5', 'cutoffs at -10 kHz and -2 kHz', 'a transition width of 500 Hz' and 'unity gain in the passband'. V6 checks only their combined effect on the output, so answers that break these stated numbers pass. Some violations cannot be observed at all: amp 1 with gain 1.5 gives the same signal, and a non-Gaussian source becomes Gaussian after band-limiting. The 500 Hz width is in effect 'anything up to about 1.5-2 kHz'. The 16 Oct policy requires every stated requirement to be checked, or else a behavioural wording. spec_properties P9 admits the checking is indirect, but the instruction does not. The same wording also hands the model the Band Pass Filter's exact parameter values, so little is left to solve except choosing complex taps and knowing GNU Radio's complex-noise amplitude convention.
findings.evidence:
./gb ladder with the unchanged task.json:
- p1_amp1_gain1p5.grc (noise amp 1, Band Pass Filter gain 1.5): V6 PASS, RMS 0.5956.
- p2_uniform_scaled.grc (complex GR_UNIFORM noise, amp 1.5*sqrt(3), RMS 1.5): V6 PASS, RMS 0.5964.
- p3_tw1500.grc (width 1500 Hz): V6 PASS, RMS 0.5831.
Near-miss mutants of the reference (run_nearmiss.py, seed 2026):
- width 1000 Hz: PASS (RMS 0.5835).
- width 1500 Hz: PASS (0.5772).
- width 2000 Hz: FAIL, but only just (0.5697 < 0.57). The author's 300-seed sweep, re-run here with build.py --sweep 300 and reproduced exactly, passes it on 267/300 seeds.
- cutoffs -9750/-2250 Hz: PASS (0.5707).
- cutoffs -10400/-1600 Hz: PASS (0.6174).
- amp 1.0 with gain 1.5: PASS (0.5883).
None of the 10 authored mutants changes the width or shifts a cutoff slightly, so the 10/10 kill rate says nothing about these numbers. 'Gaussian' cannot be graph-checked on compact answers either. graph_checks.block_present params need the key to be present, and the reference itself omits noise_type because it is the catalog default.

compliance.verdict:
The mechanical gates pass, but the item is in the wrong split and has to be moved, replaced or redesigned. Checks that hold:
- I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on 18 Oct. Solvability 10/10, 224 tokens, 3/3 variants at V6, 10 valid mutants all killed; gates.json is unchanged in content.
- I ran each mutant separately: each reaches V5 and fails V6 for the reason its 'breaks' label gives.
- The canary GUID appears only in task.json.
- id, directory and split are consistent.
- licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (an original item, not perturbed), level and family follow the rules of the time.
- It is disjoint from reports/reference/training_task_specs.json (closest is t08_run_verify_probe: noise to file plus a level probe).
- Under signature v1, build.py regenerated task.json, reference.grc and all 3 variants byte-for-byte, twice, in a scratch replica.
Problems:
- (F1, high) Under signature v1 the item lands in dev only because the inert Throttle sits after the filter. The same chain without the Throttle, or with it in its usual place, hashes to test. That conventional order is exactly gbf-test-03's reference, and the two items are template twins. Under signature v2 (compose.py, changed on 18 Oct at about 03:41 UTC, during this review) the reference hashes to test outright, and build.py now exits with 'belongs to split test, not dev'. The gates do not check the split, so gates.json still says passed.
- (F4, low) Two of the ten mutants are the same fault in this graph.

findings.claim: gbf-dev-02 does not belong in dev. Under signature v1, which was in force when it was built, it reached dev only through the position of an inert block. Its chain is noise -> band_pass_filter -> blocks_throttle2 -> file_sink. The same chain without the Throttle, or with the Throttle right after the source as usual, hashes to test, and that conventional order is exactly test item gbf-test-03's reference. This is the 'signature shopping with an inert block / block order' the split rule forbids. Under signature v2, now in src/grcbench/tier_f/compose.py, the reference signature is ('filter', 'noise'), which maps to test. That is the same signature as gbf-test-03 and all its variants, so the item now breaks the split rule outright and its build.py refuses to regenerate it. The two items are also template twins: same blocks, same instruction template, same oracle template. The dev split drives checkpoint selection and every other choice, so a dev twin of a test item carries test-specific tuning signal into those choices.
findings.evidence:
Signature v1 (signature_split_v1):
- analog_noise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_throttle2|blocks_file_sink (this reference): dev
- analog_noise_source_x|blocks_throttle2|band_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink (gbf-test-03's reference): test
- analog_noise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink (no Throttle; also variant v1's chain): test
- the old blocks_throttle gives the same pattern (after the filter: dev; before it: test)
- variant v3's chain: test
Signature v2 (compose.signature / signature_split, as of 18 Oct ~03:41 UTC):
- reference: ('filter','noise'), test
- variants v1 and v3: ('filter','noise'), test
- variant v2 (low-pass + mixer): ('filter','mix','noise'), dev
- gbf-test-03's reference and all 3 of its variants: ('filter','noise'), test
Rebuild: build.py in a scratch replica (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-02/repl, src symlinked to the repository) now exits 1 with "chain signature ('filter', 'noise') belongs to split test, not dev". The same script regenerated all files byte-identically under v1 shortly before compose.py changed.
Twin evidence: the instructions share 16 8-grams (plan tokenizer: lowercase, non-word characters to spaces), with word Jaccard 0.465, the highest pair in the first set. Shared phrases include 'transition width of 500 Hz and unity gain in the passband', 'write the filtered signal as ... samples to a File Sink whose file name is', 'at least 90 % of the power must lie between' and 'the RMS level must be about ... (within 5 %)'. The oracle template is the same: in-band >= 0.9, two stopbands < 1 %, RMS +/- 5 %, skip 4096, 65536 items. gbf-test-03's own round-1 review flagged the pair from the test side (compliance F3, medium). gates.py does not compare the task split with signature_split, so gates.json reports passed: true. task.json source.ref and cluster_id still carry the v1 signature string.
findings.suggested_fix:
Do not keep gbf-dev-02 in dev in its current form. The team decides between:
(a) drop it and author a dev replacement whose reference's v2 signature hashes to dev and whose concept is not a template twin of any test item; or
(b) move the concept to test as a sibling of gbf-test-03 with the shared cluster_id 'chain:filter|noise', so the clustered intervals count them as one cluster, and author a new dev item.
Do not rebuild the reference as low-pass + mixer just to reach ('filter','mix','noise') -> dev. That is shopping again: the natural answers, a complex band-pass, as in 2 of the 3 variants, hash to test, and the twin relation with gbf-test-03 would remain.
At set level: add a gate that fails a composed-chain task when signature_split(signature(reference)) differs from its split, and regenerate source.ref and cluster_id of every composed task with v2.

findings.claim: Two of the ten authored mutants are the same fault in this graph. m3 (bypass the filter) and m9 (rewire the File Sink to the noise source) both put the unfiltered noise in the file, so the mutation gate counts one fault class twice. The other mutants are distinct, valid and spec-breaking. Together with F3, this means the 10/10 kill rate overstates how sensitive the oracle is.
